## Statement

Let $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. Let $X$ be normed and $M\le X$ closed. Restriction $R:X^*\to M^*$ induces a linear isometric bijection $$\widetilde R:X^*/M^\perp\longrightarrow M^*,\qquad f+M^\perp\longmapsto f|_M.$$ Also $\|R\|\le1$; its norm is $1$ when $M\ne\{0\}$ and $0$ when $M=\{0\}$.

uses.excerpt: [F1] From [[thm-banach-closed-range-theorem]], with its stated hypotheses: Let $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. Assume AC and let $T:X\to Y$ be bounded linear between Banach spaces. The following are equivalent: $\operatorname{ran}T$ is norm closed; $\operatorname{ran}T^*$ is norm closed; and there is $C>0$ such that $\operatorname{dist}(x,\ker T)\le C\|Tx\|$ for all $x\in X$. In that case $\operatorname{ran}T={}^\perp(\ker T^*),\qquad \operatorname{ran}T^*=(\ker T)^\perp.$
